newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FOCUS-Russia c.bank wants stable real rouble rate.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Russia c.bank wants stable real rouble rate.

text.p: The Russian central bank will try to stop the rouble strengthening in real terms and will make it progressively more expensive for banks to buy dollars from the central bank, a senior bank official said on Thursday.
Dealers said the increase in the central bank's dollar selling rate would encourage banks not to postpone dollar purchases and thus dampen demand for roubles.

Sergei Aleksashenko, the bank's First Deputy Chairman, told Reuters Financial Television that a real appreciation of the rouble, which was partly due to the upturn in the economy, was not in Russia's economic interests.
The central bank would, therefore, stick to its policy of a gradual and pre-announced depreciation of the rouble in a currency range, known as a corridor, he said.

"The Bank of Russia will continue the practical realisation of its policy of a slow movement... in the official rate, which corresponds to the realities of the economic situation," the central bank said in a statement released simultaneously.
Aleksashenko said the current situation was similar to that in spring and summer 1995, when the rouble fell 15 percent in nominal terms over three months, while prices rose by 20 percent.
The resulting rouble appreciation in real terms hurt exporters.
"The Bank of Russia does not believe it possible to allow a repetition of this kind of influence of market forces on the rouble rate," the central bank statement said.
"It believes a currency policy aimed at maintaining the stability of the real exchange rate... is correct and corresponds to the interests of the national economy."
But foreign exchange dealers ignored his comments. Roubles for today delivery firmed to 5,744-46 per dollar from Wednesday's closing 5,750-52.

"Such announcements would move any other market but our banks could be waiting for real steps from the central bank and maybe then we will see some reaction," said United Investment Bank chief dealer Alexander Suchkov.
Dealers say strong demand for Russian Treasury bills from Russian and foreign investors is pushing up the rouble.

The policy of a sloping rouble corridor, introduced in mid-1995, allows exporters and other businessmen to predict the exchange rate over several months and provides a much-needed element of stability in economic decision-taking.
The rouble has never strayed from within the corridor or even from the central bank's own intervention rates within this.
The 1997 corridor envisages a rouble range of 5,750-6,350 to the dollar by the end of the year, compared with 5,500-6,100 at the start of the year.
Within these daily ranges the central bank sets separate bid and offer rates for its own currency market operations. The midpoint of these rates is the following day's official rate.
Aleksashenko noted that the rouble had been nudging up against the upper limit of these rates in recent weeks, approaching the level at which the central bank buys dollars.

He said the central bank had bought a net $1.5 billion from the market over the last six weeks to meet demand for roubles and would continue to intervene actively in the government securities and foreign exchange markets.

To encourage more demand for dollars, the central bank would widen the spread on its own rates, speeding up the decline of the rate at which it sells dollars for roubles, while keeping the rate at which it buys dollars declining as previously.
Since late March the central bank has been publishing daily rates with a 14-point spread. On Thursday it quoted the rouble at 5,741/5,765 per dollar.
